display.title: The Calculator: Taking Stock in the Month of Elul
display.summary_short: A baker who stops serving customers to work his calculator teaches when to make a cheshbon hanefesh, and a page with one black dot shows what to focus on in Elul.
display.summary_long: After the song, the storyteller explains that the name Elul means 'to search': it is the month to look back over the past year, at the good we did and at any mistakes, so that next year will be better, and mistakes can teach us to be more careful. He then tells the Frierdiker Rebbe's parable from Hayom Yom in a modern setting: a baker keeps customers waiting while he works out his accounts on a calculator, and a fellow storekeeper advises him to do his accounting after hours. In the same way, a Jew spends the day learning and doing mitzvos, and makes his spiritual accounting at set times: every night at the bedtime Shema, every Thursday night for the week, on Yom Kippur Katan for the month, and in Elul for the whole year. The storyteller stresses focusing more on the good than on the mistakes, and retells a teacher's experiment with a blank page bearing one black dot that everyone notices while ignoring all the white. Focusing on the good brings joy, more good deeds and Hashem's blessings, above all the Geulah.
display.lesson: Make a regular cheshbon hanefesh, especially in Elul, and focus mainly on the good you have done so that you grow with joy.
